summary: Selayar - Haji Aroeppala Airport (KSR) is a small regional airport serving Benteng, the main town on Selayar Island in Indonesia's South Sulawesi province. It functions as the primary air gateway to this remote island, which is renowned for its traditional pinisi schooner boat-building heritage and proximity to the spectacular Takabonerate National Park, one of the world's largest atoll systems. The airport supports limited domestic flights connecting the island to Makassar and other regional hubs.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate at Haji Aroeppala Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by small regional carriers offering flights to and from Makassar (UPG) in South Sulawesi. Schedules are limited and can change seasonally.

Q: How far is the airport from Benteng town center?
A: The airport is located a short drive from Benteng, typically around 10-15 minutes by car or motorbike depending on traffic and road conditions.

Q: Does the airport have international flights?
A: No, Haji Aroeppala Airport only handles domestic flights, with connections mainly to other Indonesian cities within Sulawesi.

Q: Is the airport suitable for night operations?
A: The airport has limited infrastructure and primarily operates during daylight hours, so flight schedules are generally restricted to daytime.
transport_tips: Getting to and from the airport is easiest by pre-arranged taxi or ojek (motorbike taxi), as public transport options are limited. Rental motorbikes are available in Benteng and offer flexibility for exploring the island after arrival. Allow extra time during the rainy season, as road conditions on Selayar can become challenging.
local_tip: Frequent visitors recommend flying in the morning and booking accommodation near the harbor in Benteng, as many of the best dive boats and ferries to Takabonerate National Park depart early from the waterfront the next day.
